subject: Analog Electronics
questionText: What is the knee voltage of a silicon diode?
solution: The knee voltage (or cut-in voltage) of a silicon diode is approximately 0.7V. For germanium diodes it is about 0.3V.

subject: Analog Electronics
questionText: A Zener diode is used as a
solution: A Zener diode is designed to operate in reverse breakdown and is primarily used as a voltage regulator to maintain a constant output voltage.

subject: Analog Electronics
questionText: How many PN junctions does a BJT have?
solution: A Bipolar Junction Transistor has two PN junctions: the base-emitter junction and the base-collector junction.

subject: Analog Electronics
questionText: In a common-emitter configuration the phase difference between input and output is
solution: The common-emitter amplifier introduces a 180-degree phase shift between the input and output signals.

subject: Analog Electronics
questionText: MOSFET is a
solution: MOSFET is a voltage-controlled device where the drain current is controlled by the gate-to-source voltage (Vgs).

subject: Analog Electronics
questionText: Which MOSFET can operate in both enhancement and depletion modes?
solution: A depletion-type MOSFET can operate in both enhancement mode (positive Vgs) and depletion mode (negative Vgs for N-channel).

subject: Analog Electronics
questionText: The input impedance of an ideal op-amp is
solution: An ideal operational amplifier has infinite input impedance so that it draws no current from the source.

subject: Analog Electronics
questionText: What is the gain of a non-inverting amplifier with Rf=10k and R1=2k?
solution: The gain of a non-inverting amplifier is Av = 1 + (Rf/R1) = 1 + (10k/2k) = 1 + 5 = 6.

subject: Analog Electronics
questionText: The CMRR of an ideal op-amp is
solution: The Common Mode Rejection Ratio of an ideal op-amp is infinite meaning it perfectly rejects common-mode signals.

subject: Analog Electronics
questionText: Negative feedback in an amplifier
solution: Negative feedback reduces the overall gain but increases the bandwidth and improves stability of the amplifier.

subject: Analog Electronics
questionText: The Barkhausen criterion for oscillation requires loop gain equal to
solution: For sustained oscillations the Barkhausen criterion states that the loop gain must be exactly equal to 1 and the total phase shift must be 0 or 360 degrees.

subject: Analog Electronics
questionText: A Class A power amplifier has a maximum theoretical efficiency of
solution: Class A amplifiers have a maximum theoretical efficiency of 50% when transformer-coupled and 25% when directly coupled.

subject: Analog Electronics
questionText: A low-pass filter allows frequencies
solution: A low-pass filter passes all frequencies below the cutoff frequency and attenuates frequencies above it.

subject: Digital Electronics
questionText: The output of an AND gate is HIGH only when
solution: An AND gate produces a HIGH output only when ALL of its inputs are HIGH. If any input is LOW the output is LOW.

subject: Digital Electronics
questionText: How many inputs does a NOT gate have?
solution: A NOT gate (inverter) has exactly one input. It simply inverts the input: if input is 1 output is 0 and vice versa.

subject: Digital Electronics
questionText: The output of an XOR gate with inputs A=1 and B=1 is
solution: XOR gives output 1 only when inputs are different. When both inputs are 1 (same) the output is 0.

subject: Digital Electronics
questionText: The binary equivalent of decimal 10 is
solution: To convert decimal 10 to binary: 10/2=5 R0 then 5/2=2 R1 then 2/2=1 R0 then 1/2=0 R1. Reading remainders bottom-up gives 1010.

subject: Digital Electronics
questionText: The hexadecimal equivalent of binary 11111111 is
solution: Splitting 11111111 into nibbles: 1111 = F and 1111 = F. So the hex equivalent is FF which equals 255 in decimal.

subject: Digital Electronics
questionText: A half adder has how many outputs?
solution: A half adder has two outputs: Sum (S = A XOR B) and Carry (C = A AND B).

subject: Digital Electronics
questionText: An 8-to-1 multiplexer requires how many select lines?
solution: An 8-to-1 MUX has 8 input lines = 2^3 so it needs 3 select lines to choose one of the 8 inputs.

subject: Digital Electronics
questionText: Which flip-flop is known as the delay flip-flop?
solution: The D flip-flop is called the delay flip-flop because the output Q follows the input D after one clock cycle delay.

subject: Digital Electronics
questionText: A T flip-flop with T=1 behaves as a
solution: When T=1 the T flip-flop toggles on every clock edge effectively dividing the clock frequency by 2.

subject: Digital Electronics
questionText: A 4-bit binary counter can count from
solution: A 4-bit counter has 2^4 = 16 states and counts from 0 to 15 (0000 to 1111 in binary).

subject: Digital Electronics
questionText: According to De Morgan's theorem (A+B)' equals
solution: De Morgan's first theorem states that the complement of a sum equals the product of the complements: (A+B)' = A'.B'.

subject: Digital Electronics
questionText: The simplified form of A.B + A.B' is
solution: Using the complement law: A.B + A.B' = A.(B + B') = A.1 = A. This is a fundamental Boolean simplification.

subject: Network Theory
questionText: If voltage is 12V and resistance is 4 ohms then current is
solution: By Ohm's Law I = V/R = 12/4 = 3 Amperes.

subject: Network Theory
questionText: Kirchhoff's Voltage Law states that the sum of voltages around a closed loop is
solution: KVL states that the algebraic sum of all voltages around any closed loop in a circuit is equal to zero.

subject: Network Theory
questionText: KCL is based on the law of conservation of
solution: Kirchhoff's Current Law is based on conservation of charge. The total current entering a node must equal the total current leaving it.

subject: Network Theory
questionText: Thevenin equivalent circuit consists of
optionA: Voltage source in parallel with resistance
optionB: Voltage source in series with resistance
optionC: Current source in series with resistance
solution: Thevenin's theorem states that any linear circuit can be replaced by an equivalent voltage source (Vth) in series with a resistance (Rth).

subject: Network Theory
questionText: Norton equivalent circuit consists of
optionA: Voltage source in series with resistance
optionB: Current source in parallel with resistance
optionC: Current source in series with resistance
solution: Norton's theorem replaces a circuit with an equivalent current source (In) in parallel with a resistance (Rn).

subject: Network Theory
questionText: The superposition theorem is applicable only to
solution: Superposition theorem applies only to linear circuits. It states that the response in any element is the sum of responses caused by each independent source acting alone.

subject: Network Theory
questionText: The unit of electrical power is
solution: Electrical power is measured in Watts (W). Power = Voltage x Current (P = VI).

subject: Network Theory
questionText: At resonance in a series RLC circuit the impedance is
solution: At resonance XL = XC so they cancel out. The impedance Z = R (purely resistive and minimum) allowing maximum current flow.

subject: Network Theory
questionText: The frequency of AC mains supply in India is
solution: The standard AC mains frequency in India is 50 Hz. In the USA it is 60 Hz.

subject: Network Theory
questionText: The RMS value of a sinusoidal voltage with peak value Vm is
solution: The RMS (Root Mean Square) value of a sinusoidal waveform is Vm divided by square root of 2 which is approximately 0.707 times the peak value.

subject: Network Theory
questionText: A transformer works on the principle of
solution: A transformer works on the principle of mutual electromagnetic induction between two coils sharing a common magnetic flux.

subject: Signals and Systems
questionText: A signal x(t) is even if
solution: An even signal satisfies the condition x(-t) = x(t). It is symmetric about the vertical axis. Examples include cos(t).

subject: Signals and Systems
questionText: A discrete-time signal is defined at
optionB: Only at integer values of time
solution: A discrete-time signal is defined only at discrete instants of time typically at integer values of n.

subject: Signals and Systems
questionText: The output of an LTI system is obtained by
optionA: Addition of input and impulse response
optionB: Convolution of input with impulse response
optionC: Multiplication of input and impulse response
solution: For a Linear Time-Invariant system the output y(t) = x(t) * h(t) where * denotes convolution of the input x(t) with the impulse response h(t).

subject: Signals and Systems
questionText: A system is time-invariant if
optionB: A time shift in input causes same time shift in output
solution: A time-invariant system produces the same output shape regardless of when the input is applied. A delay in input causes an identical delay in output.

subject: Signals and Systems
questionText: The Laplace transform of e^(-at).u(t) is
solution: The Laplace transform of e^(-at).u(t) is 1/(s+a) for Re(s) > -a. This is a standard transform pair.

subject: Signals and Systems
questionText: The Laplace transform of the unit step function u(t) is
solution: The Laplace transform of u(t) = integral from 0 to infinity of e^(-st) dt = 1/s for Re(s) > 0.

subject: Signals and Systems
questionText: A periodic signal can be represented using
solution: A periodic signal can be decomposed into a sum of harmonically related sinusoids using the Fourier Series representation.

subject: Signals and Systems
questionText: The Fourier series of an even function contains only
solution: An even function has symmetry about the y-axis. Its Fourier series contains only cosine terms (and possibly a DC component) since cosine is itself an even function.

subject: Signals and Systems
questionText: The Z-transform is used for analysis of
solution: The Z-transform is the discrete-time counterpart of the Laplace transform and is used for analyzing discrete-time signals and systems.

subject: Signals and Systems
questionText: According to Nyquist theorem the sampling frequency must be at least
solution: The Nyquist-Shannon sampling theorem states that to avoid aliasing the sampling rate must be at least twice the highest frequency component in the signal.

subject: Signals and Systems
questionText: Aliasing occurs when
optionB: Sampling rate is below Nyquist rate
solution: Aliasing occurs when the sampling frequency is less than twice the maximum frequency of the signal causing frequency components to overlap.

subject: Signals and Systems
questionText: Convolution in time domain is equivalent to what in frequency domain?
solution: One of the key properties of Fourier transforms is that convolution in the time domain corresponds to multiplication in the frequency domain.

subject: Signals and Systems
questionText: A causal LTI system is BIBO stable if
optionA: All poles are in the right half of s-plane
optionB: All poles are in the left half of s-plane
optionC: All poles are on the imaginary axis
solution: A causal LTI system is Bounded-Input Bounded-Output stable if and only if all poles of its transfer function lie in the left half of the s-plane (negative real parts).

subject: Signals and Systems
questionText: The impulse response of a stable system must be
solution: For BIBO stability the impulse response h(t) must be absolutely integrable i.e. the integral of |h(t)| from -infinity to infinity must be finite.
